tasks.short: Take the guest's to-go order, write it, pack it and hand it over.

steps.what: Listen to the guest and take to-go orders
Decide which substitutions the kitchen can prepare
Write the to-go order line with item and quantity
Post that to-go order line onto the kitchen ticket
Pack and prepare the to-go orders by hand
Tell the guest the to-go order is ready

tasks.design: The host still listens, decides substitutions, packs the food and tells the guest it is ready. She writes one to-go order line, with item, quantity, guest name and note, and {WORKFLOW} copies that same line onto the kitchen ticket in {OTHER}. A line with a blank item or quantity is not posted.
tasks.previous_blocker: The kitchen ticket was a second copy of a pad note, and the items existed only after she heard them.
tasks.enabler_now: A form with item, quantity, guest name and note can be copied onto the kitchen ticket once she has written those fields.
tasks.still_hard: Substitutions, packing and telling the guest stay with her. A blank item or quantity cannot be guessed.
tasks.human_edge: She hears the order, decides what the kitchen can change, and packs the food.
tasks.altitude: She still takes the order, packs it and hands it over. She writes the line once.

reach.task: Cook the to-go items on the kitchen ticket
reach.learn: Which item names and notes the cook can follow without calling back

evidence.claim: Taking a to-go order is listening, deciding substitutions, writing the items, packing the food and telling the guest it is ready. Model knowledge, E1.
Allergy notes are health data. Processing is prohibited unless an exception applies, and outside healthcare that is usually explicit consent. Record only what the kitchen needs for this visit.

assumptions: The host produces the to-go order line in s3: item, quantity, guest name and note. That writing stays at full time and is already counted in s3. {WORKFLOW} only copies that line onto the kitchen ticket. A blank item or quantity posts nothing. She does not look up a menu code.
The form replaces today's pad at the same effort. It does not shorten listening, the substitution decision, packing or telling the guest.

Prepared food is produced by the cook after reading the ticket. That cooking sits outside this task. The cook already reads a ticket, so the post is not new work for the cook. Packing uses the food, not the ticket as food.

A note that names an allergy is a kitchen instruction for this order, not a stored health profile. The guest name on the ticket is personal data. How long the ticket is kept is for the customer to set.

Focal upkeep of 0.3 hours per 100 baseline hours keeps the four fields aligned with the ticket. It is an allowance, not a measured study. If the kitchen still needs her paper slip, the saving is zero.
unknowns: What share of to-go orders is already written once on a ticket the kitchen can see.
Whether a to-go note in this restaurant ever names an allergy.
research_questions: What share of to-go orders is already written once on a ticket the kitchen can see?
Does the kitchen still require a paper slip after the ticket is posted?

already_counted.description: Writing the to-go order line before it is posted

incremental.description: Keep item, quantity, guest name and note aligned with the kitchen ticket

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Only the second copy onto the kitchen ticket is removed. Listening, substitutions, packing and telling the guest stay. Low: the kitchen still needs her paper slip, so the post does not run. High: the line she wrote is complete and only that copy disappears. This is not a measured timing study.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Tell patrons the specialties and features of the establishment.

steps.what: Read the establishment specialties on the board
Listen to what the patron asks
Decide which specialty fits this patron
Tell patrons the establishment specialties and features

tasks.design: Nothing in the conversation changes. She reads the specialties board the cook wrote before service and tells the patron the specialties and features herself. No system speaks for her.
tasks.previous_blocker: The specialty depends on what this patron asks and on what the cook wrote today.
tasks.enabler_now: The cook's board already lists today's items. She can read it and speak. No system is added.
tasks.still_hard: She has to judge which specialty fits this patron and say it herself.
tasks.human_edge: She matches the board to the person in front of her.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes. She still tells every patron the specialties.

reach.task: Write today's specialties on the board
reach.learn: Which items are sold out before she tells a patron

evidence.claim: Telling specialties is a conversation. She reads what the cook posted and says it to the patron. Model knowledge, E1.

assumptions: The specialties board (item, price, sold-out) is produced by the cook before service. She only reads it. No machine uses the sold-out flag, so that capture is not new work and is not a saving. If the board is blank she asks the cook, still inside s1 at full time.
Listening, choosing a specialty and telling the patron stay at full time. No system is built, so focal upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Whether the cook posts a specialties board before service, and who marks an item sold out.
research_questions: Does the cook post a specialties board before service, and who marks an item sold out?

incremental.description: No system is added for this conversation, so ongoing upkeep is zero

time_saved_range_pct.basis: She still tells every patron the specialties. Reading the cook's board is unchanged. No step is shorter.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Receive dining reservations and record them in the book.

steps.what: Record written dining reservations in the reservation book
Receive patrons' dining reservations by phone or door
Decide if dining reservations fit the reservation book
Record phone and walk-in dining reservations by hand
Draft reservation fields from the emailed request

loop.input: The guest's booking email, which is free text.
loop.output: Draft name, phone, date, time and covers, or a blank draft.
loop.check: The host, in the next step, compares the party, the day and the time with the email, and checks that the name is the sender's. A filled field that names a different party, day or time fails.
loop.stop: One pass. If the party, the day or the time is unclear, the draft is blank and she records the booking by phone.
loop.why_not_simpler: The email is free text. A fixed form cannot read a party size, a day and a time out of it.

steps.what: Check the party, day and time match the email
Record the checked email reservation in the reservation book

tasks.design: A complete booking is stored in the reservation book in {OTHER} only when name, phone, date, time and covers are present and the slot is inside the opening hours and covers the restaurant manager set. She still answers the phone and the door and types those reservations herself. {WORKFLOW} drafts the same five fields from a free-text booking email, and it records them only after she checks the party, the day and the time.
tasks.previous_blocker: Written requests, phone calls and free-text emails arrived in different places, and a paper book could not refuse a party outside opening hours.
tasks.enabler_now: A reservation book can store a booking only when five fields are present and the slot is open, and a bounded draft can lift those fields from an email for her to check.
tasks.still_hard: Phone and walk-in listening, party judgement and her own typing stay. An unclear email must not enter the book.
tasks.human_edge: She decides whether a large party or a closed section can be taken, and she checks that an email draft is the booking the guest asked for.
tasks.altitude: She stops retyping a complete written reservation and a second copy of an email she has checked. Phone and walk-in stay hers.

reach.task: Set opening hours and covers per slot
reach.learn: Which party sizes the book must refuse before she is asked

evidence.claim: Zenchef offers a booking widget on the restaurant site, Reserve buttons on Google and Instagram, a digital seating plan, the guest's profile and booking history shown during a phone call, a phone link that texts a booking link, and automated SMS and email reminders against no-shows.
TheFork Manager provides a reservation book, seating plans and a central guest database.

Phone and walk-in reservations are still typed by the host. A free-text booking email is not a form. The prior that software does nearly all of this task is too high, because most of the time is still the phone call and the walk-in. Model knowledge, E1.
Allergy notes are health data. Processing is prohibited unless an exception applies, and outside healthcare that is usually explicit consent. Record only what the kitchen needs for this visit.
No annex III point of the EU AI Act applies to taking bookings. Article 50(1) requires a phone or chat bot to tell callers they are dealing with AI.

Dutch WOR article 27(1)(l) requires works-council consent only if the system is also used to watch staff attendance or performance, and only where a works council exists (50 or more staff, article 2). Other countries differ.
Guest name and phone are personal data. A retention limit and a legal basis are required for a guest profile. This file does not pick the retention period. Model knowledge, E1.

assumptions: The guest produces name, phone, date, time and covers in the booking form. That typing is the customer allowance below, not her saving. If any of the five is blank, s1 stores nothing and she takes the booking by phone in s2.

The restaurant manager produces opening hours and covers per slot in the reservation book before service. That upkeep is the other-role allowance, not her saving. If those fields are missing, s1 stores nothing. The capacity rule is configuration of the book. It is not claimed as a product fact.

Existing reservations she reads in s3 are earlier bookings already in the book, not this request. Phone and walk-in fields are produced by her in s4. Nothing fills them from a guest profile. Listening and that typing stay at full time.

The email draft reads the guest's email. It does not write the book. s6 checks that the party, the day and the time are what the email asked, and that the name is the sender's. That check stays at full time and is already counted in s6. s7 records only that checked version, email-reservation-v1. A later edit is a new version and is not covered. A blank draft writes nothing.
The booking form has no allergy or medical field. No phone or chat bot is built, so the duty to tell a caller they are dealing with AI is not triggered. The draft does not talk to the guest.

The reservation book does not log her speed. It is not treated here as attendance or performance monitoring. Whether a works council exists, and whether this customer would treat the book as monitoring, is for the customer to confirm. Model knowledge on the speed log.
Guest name and phone are personal data. Retention and the legal basis are for the customer to set. This file does not pick a retention period.

The prompt prior that software does nearly all of this task is too high. The range does not use that prior, a no-show rate or a revenue figure. Reminder messages are not counted, because she has no reminder step in today's task.

Focal upkeep of 0.3 hours per 100 baseline hours keeps the five fields and the blank-field rule. It is an allowance, not a measured study. The customer and manager hours below are allowances for capture, not her saving.
unknowns: What share of bookings arrive as a complete written request, a phone call or a free-text email.
Whether a works council exists and whether this book would be treated as attendance monitoring.
How long this restaurant keeps a guest name and phone.
research_questions: What share of reservations arrive as a complete written request, a phone call or a free-text email?
Does a works council exist, and would this reservation book be treated as attendance monitoring?

already_counted.description: Checking that the party, the day and the time in the draft match the email

incremental.description: Keep the five required fields and the blank-field rule on the reservation form
Guests type name, phone, date, time and covers into the booking form. Allowance for that capture, not a measured study.
Restaurant manager keeps opening hours and covers per slot in the reservation book. Allowance for that capture, not her saving.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: High counts only part of the written-request copying and the email retype. Phone and walk-in listening, the party decision and her own typing stay in full. Low assumes almost every booking is still a phone call. This is not a no-show rate, a revenue figure, or the prior that software does nearly all of the task.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Operate the cash register to accept payments for food and beverages.

steps.what: Read the beverages bill on the cash register
Decide a split bill, a void or a dispute
Operate cash registers to accept payments
Tell the patron the amount and hand the receipt

tasks.design: She still reads the bill and accepts the payment on the cash register in {OTHER}. The waiter has already rung item, quantity and price. She does not re-enter them, and nothing takes the payment for her.
tasks.previous_blocker: The payment is taken at the register in front of the patron, including splits, voids and disputes.
tasks.enabler_now: The waiter already rings item, quantity and price, so she does not need a second entry. Nothing further is built.
tasks.still_hard: She still reads the bill, decides the exception and takes the money.
tasks.human_edge: She settles a split, a void or a dispute with the patron and takes the payment.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes. She still accepts payments at the register.

reach.learn: Which lines must be on the register before she accepts payment

evidence.claim: Accepting payment means reading the bill on the cash register, deciding a split, a void or a dispute, taking the money and handing the receipt. Model knowledge, E1.

assumptions: Bill lines (item, quantity, price) are produced by the waiter on the cash register before she takes payment. That is a prior contract, outside this task, not her saving. If the bill is empty she does not take payment. She does not re-enter the lines. No machine reads the bill for her.
Reading the bill, deciding a split, void or dispute, accepting payment and telling the amount stay at full time. No system is built, so focal upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Whether the waiter rings every line before the host takes payment.
research_questions: Does the waiter ring every line before the host takes payment?

incremental.description: No system is added for taking payment, so ongoing upkeep is zero

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Accepting payments at the register is unchanged. She still reads the bill, decides disputes and tells the patron the amount.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The week is still the door, the to-go counter and the register. She stops retyping a written reservation and a second copy of a to-go order.
reach: Cook: which item names and notes belong on a kitchen ticket.
Restaurant manager: which hours and covers per slot the book enforces.
Waiter: which bill lines are rung before payment.
skills_to_grow: Write a to-go line with item, quantity, guest name and note.
Match an email's date, time, covers and name to the draft.
Refuse a party the opening hours cannot hold.
role.ambitious_version: She still greets, packs to-go orders and takes payment. A reservation is stored only from five complete guest fields plus the manager's hours, or from a line she checked, and a blank field stores nothing.
